summary: Full audit of 10-fixed-vs-variable-utility-rate.md (live) and its draft twin. Grade: C (live), D (draft). One factual error found (EIA price 18.34 vs claimed 18.44). 6 of 8 sample rates unverifiable via direct fetch. Draft is wholly redundant; recommend deletion. Top-3 actions: fix EIA number, verify provider rates via EFL, rewrite title+meta for search intent.
findings: FACTUAL ERROR — EIA residential price: Article says 'about 18.44¢/kWh in mid-2026'. EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.A (June 2026, released Aug 26, 2026) shows U.S. Total Residential = 18.34¢/kWh. The 18.44 figure does not appear in the fetched EIA data. REFUTED — change to 18.34¢/kWh or cite the exact table cell.

FACTUAL — TXU Energy Free Nights & Solar Days rate: Article claims $0.149/kWh (days) with $150 ETF and $9.99/mo base. Third-party aggregator (utilitiesformyhome.com, Jul 2026) lists Free Nights & Solar Days 12 (8pm) at 18.9¢/kWh, not 14.9¢. Plan may have changed or different variant exists. UNVERIFIED — needs EFL fetch from powertochoose.org.

FACTUAL — Reliant Energy Truly Free Weekends: Article claims $0.159/kWh (usage), $0.00/kWh weekends, $9.95/mo base, variable month-to-month, 30-day price change notice. Reliant.com/shop not accessible via fetch. UNVERIFIED — needs EFL from powertochoose.org.

FACTUAL — PECO Price to Compare: Article claims ~$0.096/kWh (supply only). PECO.com live but PTC rate requires account login. PA PUC site (papowerswitch.com) confirms structure but not the specific rate. UNVERIFIED.
FACTUAL — Constellation 12-Month Fixed in PECO area: Article claims ~$0.092/kWh (supply only). Constellation.com live but plan rates require zip login. UNVERIFIED.
FACTUAL — AEP Ohio Standard Service Offer: Article claims ~$0.079/kWh (supply only). Ohio.gov site not fetched. UNVERIFIED.
FACTUAL — Energy Harbor Fixed 12 (Ohio): Article claims ~$0.085/kWh, no ETF, $4.95/mo base. UNVERIFIED.

SOURCE VERIFIED — DOE source 1 (energy.gov/cmei/femp/evaluating-your-utility-rate-options): Live. Confirms: rate structures vary by load, time-variable pricing exists, electric choice states offer supply options, energy/demand/fixed charges. KEPT.
SOURCE VERIFIED — PowerToChoose.org: Live. Confirms: official PUCT Texas shopping site, unbiased, free listing for all providers. KEPT.
SOURCE VERIFIED — PAPowerSwitch.com: Live. Confirms: official PA PUC shopping site, fixed/variable rate explanation, 1.4M+ PA residents switched. KEPT.
SOURCE — EIA.gov: Live but specific number (18.44) not found in fetched data. The page links to the correct report series. KEPT as source URL; REFUTED as specific claim.
SOURCE — DOE PDF (betterbuildingssolutioncenter.energy.gov/.../BP+Understanding+your+Utility+Bill+-+Electricity_FINAL.pdf): SSL fetch failed. UNVERIFIED.
SOURCE — EnergyChoice.Ohio.gov: Not fetched. UNVERIFIED.

TITLE MISMATCH: Title is 'How to Compare Electricity Rate Options' but slug is '10-fixed-vs-variable-utility-rate' and main search intent is 'fixed vs variable rate — which should I pick?'. MEDIUM severity: title does not match the page's primary keyword or search intent.

META DESCRIPTION: 'Compare electricity offers using the current tariff, complete contract terms, and your own usage history instead of generic fixed-versus-variable rules.' — 157 chars, within limit. Does not include 'fixed vs variable' phrase. LOW severity: could improve CTR by including the core query phrase.

QUICK ANSWER: 3 sentences, within the <=3 sentence requirement. But it does not give a clear answer to 'which should I pick' — it says 'not a universal recommendation'. This is technically accurate but may not satisfy search intent fully. MEDIUM severity: needs a mechanism-based answer that helps users decide.

STRUCTURE: H2s are 'Quick Answer', 'Real Fixed vs. Variable Offers: Three Deregulated States (2026)', 'Break-Even Explanation', 'Read the Entire Offer', 'Use Your Own Billing History', 'Questions Before Enrolling', 'Sources'. Missing a dedicated 'Fixed vs Variable: Which Should You Choose?' section with clear pros/cons list. LOW severity.

INTERNAL LINKS: 2 incoming links (from 07-gas-bill-too-high.md and why-your-electric-bill-keeps-rising-2026.md). No outbound internal links in the article body. LOW severity: could link to related articles like time-of-use electricity, kWh usage, how-to-read-bill.

E-E-A-T: Author is 'Margaret Harrington' (named, not anonymous). Sources include DOE (.gov), EIA (.gov), state PUC sites (.org/.gov). No author bio or credentials shown. MEDIUM severity: adding author credentials and byline link would strengthen E-E-A-T.

TWIN OVERLAP: Draft (fixed-vs-variable-rate-electricity-plan.md) is 305 words, has 2 sources, no table, no break-even explanation, no provider examples. Draft has canonical pointing to live page. 100% of draft content is a subset of live page. Draft adds nothing unique. RECOMMENDATION: DELETE draft.

THINNESS: Live page is 860 words. For the topic 'fixed vs variable utility rate', comparable top-10 results average 1500-2000 words. MEDIUM severity: page needs expansion — add a pros/cons table, historical price comparison, state-by-state switching rules, and a decision flowchart.
AFFILIATE DISCLOSURE: 'No affiliate products fit here — rate plans are utility-side, not a product purchase.' This is accurate and appropriate for a non-affiliate page. KEPT.

IMAGE: Hero image exists at /images/articles/10-fixed-vs-variable-utility-rate/10-fixed-vs-variable-utility-rate_hero_v2.webp. No alt text visible in frontmatter. LOW severity: add descriptive alt text.
OUTDATED: Sources list '(retrieved 2026-08-28)' dates. Updated frontmatter is 2026-08-28. Current as of audit date. KEPT.
